note: Versions through 0.1.2 predate this changelog; their history was not recorded.

added: A rotatable 3D surface of the log-likelihood, with the optimizer's path and the ℓ(μ) and ℓ(σ²) slices drawn on it. Drag the handle under the point to move μ and σ² together, or turn to a side view to see the profile likelihood edge-on.

A 3D view of the three tests: the likelihood surface at the chosen n, with the null hypothesis μ = μ₀ drawn across it and the geometry of the likelihood-ratio, score, and Wald tests marked on it (after Buse, 1982).
95% profile-likelihood and Wald confidence intervals below the inference figure.
A step-size slider for gradient ascent. A large step overshoots the peak, and the run stops with a note.
Before you press play, each algorithm shows where its next step would land.
Both figures can be expanded to fill the browser window.
changed: Complete rewrite in Svelte (previously React), with a new visual design.

New defaults: the sample was shifted by −0.38 so that μ̂ = 104 exactly (σ̂² is unchanged), and the null hypothesis starts at μ₀ = 96, where the three tests disagree at the .05 level. The μ₀ slider moves in whole numbers. Test statistics at a given μ₀ therefore differ from earlier versions.
The default gradient-ascent step size was halved (γ = 0.05) so the first steps no longer overshoot.
The second optimizer is now labeled Fisher scoring, which is what it always computed. Its path is unchanged.
Moving the point by hand now resets the optimizer, so the next run starts from the new point.
p-values are shown in APA style (p < .001 rather than 0.00).
removed: The contour plot and the separate ℓ(μ) and ℓ(σ²) plots. Their content is now drawn on the 3D surface. Without WebGL, the contour plot is shown instead of the surface, and the inference figure is replaced by a message; the test results and intervals are still shown.
fixed: The likelihood-ratio and score annotations now use the variance re-estimated under the null, as the tests do, rather than σ̂².

The score test's explanation said the score keeps growing as μ₀ moves away from μ̂. With the variance re-estimated under the null, it shrinks again far from μ̂, while the test statistic keeps growing.
The density curve on the sample plot is now accurate in the tails when σ² is small.
